Hypothesis (data-grounded): In replicated Psychology studies (Many Labs / rpp project), the most-senior author on the replication side is a junior professor (Assistant Professor) in roughly 29% of cases. Specifically, among the 35 replicated Psychology studies, 10 have a most-senior replication author at the Assistant Professor rank, giving a proportion of 10/35 ≈ 0.286 (28.6%).

Definition used (per researcher approval, reading A): "junior professors" = seniority.r == "Assistant Professor" (the junior-most explicit professor rank). "Assistant" was deliberately EXCLUDED because it more likely denotes a non-faculty research assistant.

Workflow: (1) Loaded meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv (927 rows). (2) Filtered to project=='rpp' (Psychology) → 97 rows. (3) Filtered to replicated=='1' → 35 rows (denominator). (4) Counted rows with seniority.r=='Assistant Professor' → 10 (numerator). (5) Proportion = 10/35 = 0.2857.

payload.hypothesis: In replicated Psychology (rpp) studies, the proportion whose most-senior replication author is a junior professor (defined as 'Assistant Professor') is 10/35 ≈ 0.286 (28.6%).
payload.definition: junior professor = seniority.r == 'Assistant Professor' (reading A; 'Assistant' excluded as likely non-faculty)
payload.workflow: Filtered study-data CSV to project=='rpp' AND replicated=='1' (35 rows), counted seniority.r=='Assistant Professor' (10 rows), proportion = 10/35.
